title: Response to Feedback on Roll-out of ERP 2.0 On-Board Unit for Vehicles
what_it_is: Response to Feedback on Roll-out of ERP 2.0 On-Board Unit for Vehicles

sections.label: ERP system lifespan ending
sections.summary: The current Electronic Road Pricing system will reach the end of its operational lifespan in a few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The current Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) system will reach the end of its operational lifespan in a few years.

sections.label: OBU installation numbers
sections.summary: About 2% or 18,000 vehicles out of almost one million vehicles in Singapore have installed the OBU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: About 2% or 18,000 vehicles out of almost one million vehicles in Singapore have installed the OBU.

sections.label: Touch-screen display option
sections.summary: Before installing the OBU, vehicle owners will be given the option to decide if they want to install the touch-screen display.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Before installing the OBU, vehicle owners will be given the option to decide if they want to install the touch-screen display.

sections.label: Processing unit driver side option
sections.summary: LTA has expanded the option for vehicle owners to install the processing unit on the driver side, subject to technical feasibility.

sentences.text: Taking on board feedback from the early adopters, LTA has expanded the option for vehicle owners to install the processing unit on the driver side if they wish to do so, subject to technical feasibility.

sections.label: ERP 2.0 CEPAS card improvement
sections.summary: LTA has worked with partners to improve ERP 2.0 so motorists need not remove their CEPAS card from the processing unit while driving.

sentences.text: LTA has worked with its partners to improve the ERP 2.0 system, so that motorists do not need to remove their CEPAS card from the processing unit when they are driving the vehicle.

sections.label: Notifications for road safety zones
sections.summary: Early adopters find notifications for bus lanes, Silver Zones and School Zones useful, and LTA is working to expand the list.

sentences.text: Early adopters have shared with LTA that they find the notifications for bus lanes, Silver Zones and School Zones useful, as these increase their situational awareness and improve road safety.

We are working with partners to expand the list, including with the Traffic Police to include notifications for speed camera zones, with the intent of enhancing road safety by reminding motorists to keep within the speed limits at these locations.

sections.label: OBU design and feedback
sections.summary: An MP asks whether MOT will improve the OBU design from user feedback and whether it runs an active feedback programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first supplementary question is: there are a lot of reports that came out immediately after the ERP 2.0 release on social media, as well as one that came out just today in CNA, talking about how the installation is not so straightforward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even now, with it being allowed for the OBU to be installed it at the driver's footwell, some car makes are a bit smaller, especially Japanese cars, so, the footwell may not be the best location – drivers may still hit against the unit as they drive or as they get in and out of the car.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am just wondering whether MOT will continue to improve upon the current design, based on feedback from users, and introduce a different model?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second supplementary question is: as we launched this OBU on 1 May, is there an active survey or feedback programme by MOT to actively collect feedback from all the motorists that have had the OBU installed?

sections.label: Dashboard and footwell temperatures
sections.summary: Footwell temperatures reach about 38 to 39 degrees, while dashboard temperatures reach 50 to 52 degrees, risking overheating for a single-piece OBU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But for the footwell, it could go up to about 38 to 39 degrees, because it is an enclosed space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But on the dashboard, it will go as high as 50 to 52 degrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: With this kind of temperature, if you were to put a single-piece OBU – that means the antenna, the display and the processing unit, all on the dashboard – there is a risk that it could overheat.

sections.label: Free OBU reconfiguration offered
sections.summary: Motorists who previously had the OBU on the passenger side can now switch to the driver's side free of charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For example, because previously we only allowed them to put it on a passenger side; if some of them now say "I want to put you on the driver's side", we will do the switch for them for free.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think that is fair, because when they installed earlier, there was no option given to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if some of them now want to do it, we will offer this reconfiguration for them, free of charge.

sections.label: Distance-based charging option
sections.summary: ERP 2.0 gives the option of distance-based charging, with impact on user groups and overall societal benefit to be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: What ERP 2.0 gives us is the option to do distance-based charging if we wish to do so, and if in the process of doing that, certainly we need to consider the impact on different groups of users and, overall, what is the benefit to society.

sections.label: Smartphone security and tampering
sections.summary: A smartphone system cannot assure the same data, systems and tamper-resistance security, so it cannot fulfil all ERP 2.0 features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And a phone, depending on the model that you use and the software, and the apps that you install, I do not think you can be assured of the same level of data security and systems security, including against tampering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, for all those reasons, a smartphone system would not be able to fulfil all the features and functionalities of what we want to achieve with ERP 2.0.

sections.label: OBU meets AEC-Q100 standard
sections.summary: An MP asks the Minister to confirm the new OBU meets the Automotive Electronics Council Q100 reliability standard for Singapore's climate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just one quick supplementary question for the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note the Minister's explanation about temperature being the reason why we cannot have the one-piece design on cars, but I just wanted to confirm that this new OBU actually meets the minimum grade force standard of the Automotive Electronics Council Q100 requirements for reliable operations in Singapore's climate.
